# Unique usernames

Implement `Registry` in `solution.py`, keeping all state in `runtime.Store` (see
`runtime.py`). Each user holds at most one name, and each name belongs to at most one
user.

```python
Registry(store)
register(user: str, name: str) -> bool
rename(user: str, new_name: str) -> bool
owner(name: str) -> str | None
name_of(user: str) -> str | None
```

- Names are 1 to 16 characters from `a-z`, `0-9` and `-`, compared case-insensitively:
  `Bob` and `bob` are the same name. Store and return names in lower case. Calls with
  an invalid name return `False` (or `None` for `owner`) and change nothing.
- `register` gives `user` the name if the user has no name and nobody holds the name.
  Registering the name the user already holds returns `True`. Otherwise `False`.
- `rename` moves a user who holds a name to `new_name` if nobody else holds it; the
  old name becomes free. Renaming to the name the user already holds returns `True`.
  On `False`, nothing changes.
- `owner` and `name_of` return the current holder and name.
- Many `Registry` objects in many threads may share one `Store`. Calls for the same
  user never overlap; calls for different users may. When no call is in progress,
  `owner(n) == u` exactly when `name_of(u) == n`.

Use P to model the design before implementing it, and to test the implementation.
`snappea` and the `pysnappea` Python package are installed. Keep your P files and
tests in this directory; the tests must run with `python -m pytest`.
----
---
name: p-modeling
description: Design concurrent or retrying code with a P model checked by snappea, then test the real implementation against what the model found.
---

# P modeling

P finds bugs that only appear in some orderings: two clients read the same version,
a retry arrives after the state changed, a step fails between read and write. Use it
for shared state, retries, concurrency and recovery. Pure transformations need only
ordinary tests.

The model is worth what it changes in the code and tests. Follow these steps in order.

## 1. List the risks (before any code)

Write down, in `DESIGN.md`:

- the contract in checkable sentences ("a retried request returns its first result and
  has no further effect");
- the real atomic primitives (one compare-and-swap on one key, a lock, a transaction).
  Everything else can interleave;
- 5-10 concrete scenarios that could break the contract. Always consider:
  two clients that read the same version; a retry after another request changed the
  state (including retries of rejected or empty results); two objects sharing one
  store; each precondition false on its own; values exactly at each boundary.

## 2. Model the algorithm, not the API

- One machine for the store, holding exactly what the real store holds. Its handlers
  are the real primitives: `load` replies with (version, value); `cas` succeeds only at
  the current version.
- Client machines run your algorithm: send load, receive, decide, send cas, retry on
  failure. Every `send`/`receive` is a point where another client can run. If the
  whole operation is one handler, the model assumes the race away.
- A `spec` monitor computes the expected results from the contract and the history of
  requests, independently of the algorithm, and asserts each actual result.
- Drive it with 2-3 clients and small `choose(n)` inputs, plus fixed tests for the
  scenarios from step 1. Start from the [syntax reference](reference/p-patterns.md)
  and [CAS + retries example](examples/cas-retry/Balance.p).

## 3. Check until it passes for real

```sh
snappea check            # every test case, then coverage and mutation checks
```

- Exit 1 is work to do: a bug (fix the design; keep the scenario), a coverage gap
  (add a scenario), or a surviving mutant (an assertion is missing). Read each one.
- Do not finish with `--no-mutation` or `--allow-incomplete-coverage`. Use them only
  while iterating. If search is incomplete, shrink the bounds or raise `--timeout`.
- A bug found here is the payoff: write it down, fix the design, then implement.

## 4. Implement, then test what the model explored

Read [testing the implementation](guides/testing-implementation.md). For each
scenario and each bug the model found, write a Python test that makes it happen on the
real code. Random thread stress rarely hits a race; force it:

- wrap the store so a competing call runs between this call's load and its
  compare-and-swap, or so two calls read the same version before either writes;
- retry a request after another request changed the state, through a second object.

Add an observation test: run real calls, record their actual arguments and results as
events, and check them against your P spec with `snappea.check_events` (install
`pysnappea`, `import snappea`). See [implementation](guides/implementation.md).

## 5. Prove the tests can fail

Break your implementation on purpose, one change at a time (ignore the
compare-and-swap result, drop a retry memo, flip a boundary `<` to `<=`, keep state
in the object instead of the store). Run the tests each time; every break must fail a
test. Add a test for any that pass. Restore the code.

## Done means

- `snappea check` exits 0, with complete search or stated bounds.
- `python -m pytest` passes, including forced-interleaving and observation tests.
- Every hand-made break from step 5 fails a test.
- `DESIGN.md` states the contract, primitives, scenarios, model bounds, what the model
  found, and what is not covered.

## References

- [Syntax and commands](reference/p-patterns.md), [modeling](guides/modeling.md),
  [scenarios and oracles](guides/scenarios-and-oracles.md), [recovery](guides/recovery.md).
- Examples: [CAS + generated retries](examples/cas-retry/Balance.p),
  [reservation + Python tests](examples/reservation/Reservation.p),
  [generated histories](examples/bounded-history/bounded-history.p),
  [durable retry](examples/durable-retry/DurableRetry.p),
  [versioned publication](examples/versioned-publication/Revalidated.p).

import threading
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor

import pytest
from snappea import check_events

from runtime import Store
from solution import Registry


class Hook:
    """Store wrapper: run callbacks right after the n-th matching load, and/or
    make loads of a key wait on a barrier so two callers read the same version."""

    def __init__(self, inner):
        self.inner = inner
        self.after_load = []   # (predicate(key), callback) one-shot
        self.barrier_keys = {}  # key -> Barrier

    def load(self, key):
        result = self.inner.load(key)
        b = self.barrier_keys.get(key)
        if b is not None:
            b.wait(timeout=5)
        for i, (pred, cb) in enumerate(self.after_load):
            if pred(key):
                del self.after_load[i]
                cb()
                break
        return result

    def compare_swap(self, key, version, value):
        return self.inner.compare_swap(key, version, value)


def consistent(reg, users, names):
    for u in users:
        n = reg.name_of(u)
        if n is not None:
            assert reg.owner(n) == u
    for n in names:
        o = reg.owner(n)
        if o is not None:
            assert reg.name_of(o) == n


# ---- sequential contract ----

def test_basic_and_case():
    r = Registry(Store())
    assert r.register("a", "Bob")
    assert r.owner("BOB") == "a" and r.name_of("a") == "bob"
    assert not r.register("b", "bOb")
    assert r.register("a", "BOB")           # same name again
    assert not r.register("a", "other")      # already has a name
    assert r.name_of("a") == "bob" and r.owner("other") is None
    assert r.name_of("nobody") is None and r.owner("zzz") is None


def test_rename():
    r = Registry(Store())
    assert not r.rename("a", "x")            # no name yet
    assert r.name_of("a") is None and r.owner("x") is None
    r.register("a", "one")
    r.register("b", "two")
    assert not r.rename("a", "TWO")
    assert r.name_of("a") == "one" and r.owner("one") == "a" and r.owner("two") == "b"
    assert r.rename("a", "ONE")              # own name
    assert r.rename("a", "three")
    assert r.owner("one") is None and r.owner("three") == "a"
    assert r.register("c", "one")            # old name is free
    assert r.rename("b", "one") is False


def test_validation_boundaries():
    r = Registry(Store())
    assert r.register("a", "x" * 16)
    assert not r.register("b", "x" * 17)
    assert not r.register("b", "")
    assert r.register("b", "-")
    assert r.register("c", "a-9")
    for bad in ["a b", "a_b", "é", "a\n", "K", "ａ", "a.b", None, 5]:
        assert not r.register("d", bad), bad
        assert r.owner(bad) is None
        assert r.name_of("d") is None
    assert not r.rename("a", "y" * 17) and r.name_of("a") == "x" * 16
    assert not r.rename("a", "bad name") and r.name_of("a") == "x" * 16
    assert r.owner("y" * 17) is None and r.owner("") is None


def test_invalid_rename_keeps_name():
    r = Registry(Store())
    r.register("a", "ok")
    assert not r.rename("a", "NOT OK")
    assert r.name_of("a") == "ok" and r.owner("ok") == "a"


def test_two_registries_share_store():
    s = Store()
    r1, r2 = Registry(s), Registry(s)
    assert r1.register("a", "n")
    assert not r2.register("b", "N")

        reg = Registry(s)

            n = names[(i * 7 + hash(u)) % 4]
            if i % 3 == 0:

class Recorder:
    """Emits the spec's events at the real store's commit points."""

    NAMES = {"a": 0, "b": 1}
    USERS = {"u0": 0, "u1": 1}

    def __init__(self):
        self.inner = Store()
        self.events = []

    def load(self, key):
        return self.inner.load(key)

    def compare_swap(self, key, version, value):
        _, prev = self.inner.load(key)
        ok = self.inner.compare_swap(key, version, value)
        if ok:
            kind, k = key
            if kind == "name" and value is not None:
                self.ev("eClaimed", user=self.USERS[value], name=self.NAMES[k])
            elif kind == "name":
                self.ev("eReleased", user=self.USERS[prev], name=self.NAMES[k])
            else:
                self.ev("eCommitted", user=self.USERS[k], name=self.NAMES[value])
        return ok

    def ev(self, name, **payload):
        self.events.append({"event": name, "payload": payload})


def finish(rec, reg):
    """Done events then public reads, as the model's quiescent phase does."""
    rec.ev("eClientDone")
    rec.ev("eClientDone")
    for u, ui in Recorder.USERS.items():
        n = reg.name_of(u)
        owners = [reg.owner(x) for x in ("a", "b")]
        rec.ev("eFinal", user=ui,
               ownerOf0=Recorder.USERS.get(owners[0], -1),
               ownerOf1=Recorder.USERS.get(owners[1], -1),
               nameOf=Recorder.NAMES.get(n, -1))

    rec.ev("eClaimRejected", user=Recorder.USERS[user], name=Recorder.NAMES[name])
    rec.ev("eRejectedReply", user=Recorder.USERS[user], name=Recorder.NAMES[name])

# Unique usernames: design

Files: `solution.py` (implementation), `Names.p` (P model + spec `UniqueNames`),
`test_registry.py` (pytest), `runtime.py` (given store).

## Contract

- A user holds at most one name; a name belongs to at most one user.
- Names are 1-16 chars of `a-z0-9-`, case-insensitive (ASCII only), stored lower case.
  Invalid names: `False` / `None`, no change.
- `register`: succeeds iff user has no name and the name is free; repeating the
  user's own name is `True`; otherwise `False`.
- `rename`: needs a held name; succeeds iff the new name is free or already the user's;
  the old name becomes free. `False` changes nothing.
- When no call is running, `owner(n) == u` iff `name_of(u) == n`.
- Calls for one user never overlap; calls for different users and Registry objects may.

## Primitives

Per-key `load` and `compare_swap` only; no cross-key transaction. So a name change
touching `name:n` and `user:u` is several steps and other users interleave.

Records (all in the Store, nothing in the object):

- `("name", n)` -> owning user or `None` (freed names are written `None`, never deleted,
  so versions only grow).
- `("user", u)` -> the user's name or `None`. Only `u`'s own calls write it.

Algorithm:

- register: read `user:u`; if named, return `name == it`. Claim `name:n` by CAS from a
  free read (retry on lost race, reject if a read shows another holder). Then write `user:u`.
- rename: read `user:u` (old). Claim `name:new`; write `user:u = new`; then free `name:old`.
  Order matters: a name is claimed before the user points at it and freed after the user
  stops pointing at it, so no name is ever held by two users and `name_of` never points
  at a name another user owns. Between steps `owner(old)` still says `u` while
  `name_of(u)` says new: a transient, allowed only while the call is in progress.

## Scenarios (each has a test)

1. Two users register the same name, both reading it free (forced same version): one wins.
2. A competitor takes the name between this call's read and CAS: CAS fails, re-read, reject.
3. Same for a rename to a taken name: user keeps old name, old name still owned.
4. Name freed by a rename, then registered by someone else; a retry after the change succeeds.
5. Name freed and retaken between read and CAS (ABA): version check rejects.
6. Two users rename to each other's names, same-version reads: both `False`, nothing moves.
7. Boundaries: lengths 0, 1, 16, 17; `-`; uppercase; spaces, `_`, non-ASCII, Kelvin sign
   (lowers to `k`), trailing newline, `None`, int.
8. Each precondition false alone: has other name; name held; no name for rename; invalid name
   on rename (old name kept).
9. Second `Registry` on the same store sees and conflicts with the first (state in Store).
10. Thread stress with many users/names: invariant and uniqueness at the end.

## Model (`Names.p`)

Store machine with versioned keys, `eLoad` / `eCas`; two `User` machines, each doing
two operations (step 1 is register or rename, step 2 is register or rename, names 0/1 chosen
by `choose(2)`), then a barrier and public reads. Spec `UniqueNames` is independent of the
algorithm: it follows commits announced by the store at the CAS, checks name never claimed
while held, rejections only when a probe saw another holder, successes hold the name,
rejected register/rename have a cause, every user completed its ops, and after quiescence
`owner`/`name_of` agree and match the spec. Bounds: 2 users, 2 names, 2 ops each, one store;
search is complete (about 100k schedules, ~12 s). Claim retry is bounded by an assertion
(`tries <= 3`) so a livelock is a failure.

## What the model found

- Modeling errors only (announce ordering at the client instead of the store commit point,
  reads before quiescence). The algorithm passed once the oracle was correct; the
  claim-before-point, free-after-repoint order was chosen up front because the reverse
  (free old first, or point user before claim) breaks uniqueness or loses the old name on a
  failed rename; both reverse orders are tested as deliberate breaks and fail tests.

## Not covered

- Crashes between steps (a crash after claim leaves a name held by a user with no
  name; there is no recovery). Out of scope: calls complete.
- More than 2 users / names in the model; Python stress covers more but not exhaustively.
- Overlapping calls for the same user (excluded by the contract).
- Python observation test checks sequential/forced histories only.
- Some `snappea check` mutants survive within the mutation time limit: equivalent ones
  (defaults such as `step = 0`, `res = false`, `cur = 0`, version `+1` vs `-1`), and a few
  whose search was incomplete in the time limit. Treat with that caveat.
- An equivalent variant (fail a rename/register when the single claim CAS loses, instead
  of retrying) is also linearizable; tests do not require retrying.
EOF
